# awscc_networkmonitor_monitor (Resource)

An Amazon CloudWatch Network Monitor resource that monitors network traffic between a source VPC subnet and a destination IP address.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `monitor_name` (String) The name identifying the monitor. It can contain only letters, underscores (_), or dashes (-), and can be up to 200 characters.

### Optional

- `aggregation_period` (Number) The time, in seconds, that metrics are aggregated and sent to Amazon CloudWatch. Valid values are either 30 or 60.
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags for the monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The time and date when the monitor was created.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `modified_at` (String) The time and date when the monitor was last modified.
- `monitor_arn` (String) The ARN of the monitor.
- `state` (String) The state of the monitor.

<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Optional:

- `key` (String)
- `value` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_networkmonitor_monitor.example
  identity = {
    monitor_arn = "monitor_arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `monitor_arn` (String) The ARN of the monitor

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_networkmonitor_monitor.example
  id = "monitor_arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_networkmonitor_monitor.example "monitor_arn"
```
